headline: West Virginia State Park and Refuge Access
reservation: Canaan Valley Resort and Blackwater Falls State Parks do not require permits for general entry, but lodging and developed campsites should be booked via the West Virginia State Parks portal. Winter ski rentals and summer horseback tours operate on independent systems; verify current availability and seasonal opening dates through the official resort website.

days.title: Falls and Canyon Overlooks

stops.name: Blackwater Falls
stops.detail: View the amber-tinted waters from the boardwalks and descend the stairs for a close-up of the gorge.

stops.name: Lindy Point
stops.detail: Walk the easy forest trail to a wooden platform overlooking the deep Blackwater Canyon.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for park travel; roads are paved but can be icy in late autumn.
days.note: The stairs to the falls can be slippery when wet; use the Gentle Trail for an accessible viewpoint.

days.title: High Highland Bogs and Meadows

stops.name: Freeland Boardwalk
stops.detail: Walk through the Canaan Valley National Wildlife Refuge to see rare wetland plants and migrating birds.

stops.name: Canaan Valley Scenic Chairlift
stops.detail: Ride to the top of the ridge for a panoramic view of the entire 14-mile-long valley.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours for regional travel; roads between Davis and the refuge are well-maintained.
days.note: Check the Wildlife Refuge website for seasonal hunting closures which may affect trail access.

days.title: Tundra Landscapes and Art

stops.name: Bear Rocks Preserve
stops.detail: Explore the windswept quartz boulders and stunted spruce trees of the Dolly Sods plateau.

stops.name: Front Street, Thomas
stops.detail: Visit the galleries and historic architecture of this former coal town before departure.

days.driving: Allow 2.5 hours for the drive to MGW airport; Dolly Sods roads are unpaved and slow.
days.note: Dolly Sods is extremely exposed to weather; temperatures are often 10-15 degrees cooler than the valley floor.

intel.title: Dolly Sods Limits
intel.text: The Bear Rocks parking area is small and often overflows onto the road shoulder during peak fall foliage. Visit midweek to ensure a spot and avoid long walks on the gravel road.

intel.title: Mountain Topography
intel.text: Cell service is unavailable in most of the Wildlife Refuge and Dolly Sods Wilderness. Paper maps are recommended as GPS often fails in the deep valleys.

intel.title: Gateway Fuel Stops
intel.text: Davis and Thomas are the last reliable spots for fuel before heading into the Monongahela National Forest. Ensure you have enough gas for the slow, high-elevation climbing required to reach the Sods.

intel.title: Seasonal Road Closures
intel.text: Forest Road 37 and Forest Road 75 leading to Dolly Sods are typically closed from January through mid-April. Always check the U.S. Forest Service alerts for winter gate status.

intel.title: Peat Bog Protection
intel.text: The wetlands in the refuge are extremely fragile; staying on the boardwalks is required by law to prevent damage to rare balsam fir and sphagnum moss.

plan.arrival: Arrive at Morgantown (MGW), rent a vehicle, and stop in Morgantown or Davis for mountain-ready supplies and snacks.
plan.vehicle: A standard vehicle works for most valley sites, but an AWD or 4WD vehicle is highly recommended for the unpaved forest roads leading to Dolly Sods.
plan.goldenHour: Lindy Point is the premier sunset location for canyon views, while Bear Rocks offers exceptional sunrise light across the Allegheny Front.
